name: Riyadh
tagline: Desert capital, mud-brick Diriyah and the Edge of the World
summary: The fast-changing Saudi capital, with the restored mud-brick birthplace of the Saudi state at Diriyah, good museums and the cliffs of the Tuwaiq escarpment an hour away.
seasonNote: Summer passes 45°C; Riyadh Season brings concerts and festivals from October to March.
arrival: King Khalid International Airport is 35 km north; taxis and the Riyadh Metro line 4 link the city.
gettingAround: Use the Riyadh Metro, ride-hailing apps or a car; the city is spread out and not walkable.
foodTip: Najdi dishes: jareesh (cracked wheat), kabsa, margoog stew and qursan, with Saudi coffee and dates.
buyTip: Oud perfume, dates and Bedouin crafts in the souqs around Masmak.
baseArea: Olaya for hotels and restaurants, or near Diriyah

connections.note: Frequent flights; a train link is under construction.

items.name: At-Turaif, Diriyah
items.summary: The mud-brick palaces of the first Saudi capital, restored with museums and light shows.
items.expect: Ticketed evening visits; much of Diriyah is still under construction.
items.tip: Go at sunset, then eat at the Bujairi Terrace across the wadi.

items.name: Edge of the World
items.summary: Sheer 300-metre cliffs of the Tuwaiq escarpment with a view over an ancient caravan plain.
items.expect: About 90 minutes each way, the last part on rough desert track; 4x4 or tour only. Closed in hot months.
items.tip: Go with a tour for sunset and a picnic dinner.
